rules.title: Grammar & Vocabulary — Exam Rule
rules.rule: Read the complete sentence first. Identify the grammar point being tested, eliminate clearly wrong choices, then check tense, agreement, articles, prepositions, conjunctions and meaning before selecting the answer.
rules.tip: Do not choose an option only because it sounds familiar; check the sentence as a whole.

rules.title: Analogy — How to solve
rules.rule: An analogy expresses a relationship between two words or ideas. Identify the exact relationship in the first pair (for example, person–place, tool–function, whole–part or cause–effect) and reproduce the same relationship in the second pair.
rules.tip: Write the missing word/phrase directly. Analogy is a relationship-completion question, not a multiple-choice question.

rules.title: Rewrite as Directed — Rule
rules.rule: First identify the instruction: voice, reported speech, degree, question form, conjunction, simple/compound/complex sentence or another transformation. Preserve the original meaning while changing only the required structure.
rules.tip: After rewriting, check tense, subject–verb agreement, pronouns, punctuation and whether the original meaning is unchanged.

rules.title: Reported Speech — Rule
rules.rule: In reported speech, change pronouns and relevant tense/time expressions according to the reporting verb and context. Questions normally change to statement word order; use whether/if for yes-no questions and retain the appropriate wh-word for wh-questions.
rules.tip: Do not use question word order inside the reported clause.

rules.title: Active and Passive Voice — Rule
rules.rule: In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject. Use the correct form of be + past participle (V3), and add by + agent when the agent is needed.
rules.tip: Keep the tense unchanged while changing the structure.

rules.title: Degrees of Comparison — Rule
rules.rule: Positive, comparative and superlative forms can be transformed without changing meaning. Watch for structures such as as…as, than, the + superlative and one of the + superlative.
rules.tip: Keep the comparison and its meaning exactly the same after transformation.

rules.title: Tenses — Rule
rules.rule: Use the tense that matches the time and context. Check time markers, sequence of events and subject–verb agreement before changing a verb form.
rules.tip: A tense change must still preserve the intended time relationship.

rules.title: Articles — Rule
rules.rule: Use a/an for a non-specific singular countable noun and the for a specific or already identified noun. No article is often used for plural or uncountable nouns when speaking generally.
rules.tip: Choose a or an by sound, not simply by the first written letter.

rules.title: Prepositions — Rule
rules.rule: Prepositions show relationships of time, place, direction and other connections. Select the preposition that fits the expression and the meaning of the complete sentence.
rules.tip: Learn common fixed combinations such as interested in, depend on and good at.

rules.title: Subject–Verb Agreement — Rule
rules.rule: A singular subject generally takes a singular verb and a plural subject takes a plural verb. Ignore intervening phrases when identifying the true subject.
rules.tip: Words between the subject and verb do not change the number of the subject.
